answer: Walk-crossing admission: each epoch's beacon seeds random walks over the trust graph. Every verifier flies one falcon of 400 hops; a newcomer is admitted only where that falcon lands on its trail, one slot per landing. A sybil pocket is low-conductance: walks orbit inside, the falcon rarely enters, so crossings scale with rim width, not pocket size. Nine hundred heads need nine hundred landings; the rim only widens with new copper, every copper strand a distinct aged counterparty the attacker cannot duplicate. Rotating beacons kill precomputed routes; isolation is the toll booth.
